perturbations.a: Millions of babies and youngsters are subjected to anesthesia every year during medical treatment. Sevoflurane is a volatile anesthetic that is commonly utilized for pediatric anesthesia. However, earlier reports have indicated that the administration of sevoflurane promotes neurodegeneration, raising concerns regarding the safety of its application. The present examination aimed to explore caffeic acid phenethyl ester (CAPE) and its protective effect against sevoflurane‑induced neurotoxicity in newborn rats. Rat pups were administered with CAPE at 10, 20 or 40 mg/kg body weight from postnatal day 1 (P1) to P15. The P7 rats were subjected to sevoflurane (2.9%) for 6 h. Control group rats received no sevoflurane or CAPE. Neuronal apoptosis was assessed by terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase dUTP nick‑end labeling assay. The expression levels of caspases (caspase‑3, ‑8 and ‑9), apoptotic pathway proteins [Bcl‑2‑associated X protein (Bax), B cell CCL/lymphoma 2 (Bcl‑2), Bcl‑2‑like 1 (Bcl‑xL), Bcl‑2‑associated agonist of cell death (Bad) and phosphorylated (p)‑Bad], mitogen‑activated protein kinases (MAPK) signaling pathway proteins [c‑Jun N‑terminal kinase (JNK), p‑JNK, extracellular signal‑regulated kinase (ERK)1/2, p‑ERK1/2, p38, p‑p38 and p‑c‑Jun] and the phosphoinositide 3‑kinase (PI3K)/Akt cascade were evaluated by western blotting following sevoflurane and CAPE treatment. In addition, the expression of cleaved caspase‑3 was examined by immunohistochemistry. CAPE significantly diminished sevoflurane‑induced apoptosis, downregulated the expression levels of caspases and pro‑apoptotic proteins (Bax and Bad) and elevated the expression levels of Bcl‑2 and Bcl‑xL when compared with sevoflurane treatment. Furthermore, CAPE appeared to alter the expression levels of MAPKs and activate the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway. Thus, the present examination illustrated that CAPE effectively inhibited sevoflurane‑induced neuroapoptosis by modulating the expression and phosphorylation of apoptotic pathway proteins and MAPKs, and by regulating the PI3K/Akt pathway.

This year, everything will alter. The Berlin-based Danish vocalist, songwriter and producer Asbjørn is leading a whole new, unfettered generation of young pop performers: With his daring sound, the charismatic pop icon is here to renovate dusty male genre clichés and bring BOY POWER to the pop universe, providing it a whole new appearance for 2018: Pøp 3.0!  
Asbjørn crafts pop with an essential message. „I think it’s high moment we guys remake pop music from our perspective. I want to demonstrate that there are an infinite number of methods to articulate one’s masculinity – without reverting to age-old clichés. We should finally toss all these gender biases overboard and be who we desire to be”  

With a focus on variety and transparency, Asbjørn’s music is vibrant, thrilling and unpredictably catchy – ‘Nothing2Lose’ being the ideal example. Asbjørn states: “The song was composed during the wildest summer of my existence. Three intense months that felt like a single, extraordinary festival. Including wild bashes, bad hangovers and all the highs and lows that are just part of it when you’re in love. There was nothing else around us but him and me. Together, we enjoyed the endless summer evenings in Berlin and felt endlessly liberated. The lyrics have something eternal; this tune is the soundtrack to an unforgettable life that I’ll never recall. „  
Asbjørn’s narrative begins as a young lad, stood in his Danish house in front the mirror, performing his beloved songs and imagined choreography. He realized early-on the incredible influence of pop music. Starting with pop legends from the 90s including Spice Girls, Backstreet Boys and Max Martin, via R&B giants such as Destiny`s Child, Missy Elliott and Timbaland, to melancholic modern electronic pop performers like Robyn and Lykke Li, Asbjørn draws multiple inspirations, which he interlaces into his distinctive signature sound. At just 19, he established his own label, where he independently released two highly praised albums. Today, his clips command millions of views, with almost 40,000 followers to his YouTube channel.  
Following recent live performances at the Montreux Jazz Festival, Reeperbahn Festival, Berlin Festival, London’s Ja Ja Ja Festival, and Electronic Beats Festival, the 25-year-old Scandinavian is poised for another hectic summer with lots of forthcoming shows to be declared. He is currently crafting his forthcoming album ‘BOY PWR’.

Went to County Hall instead of City Hall. Misguided by event info. Great 40 min stroll… #errordiary

  1. More from @annblandford: I was an hour late for a meeting this evening because I went to County Hall when I should have gone to City Hall. I just pieced together how this transpired. Looking at the map on the eventbrite page (see link to pic above) the ‘target’ marker is right by County Hall. I can only presume that I was the only person who actually utilized this map to get to the meeting as other participants went to City Hall.
    Which leaves me with three inquiries:
    1. What details did everyone else use to get to City Hall? Did everyone else know where it is without a map?
    2. What did the individual who configured the eventbrite page do to create the wrong map? (The answer seems to be that the mistake is with Google, because very slight adjustments in the Google Maps query alters where it directs to. I won’t bore you with the specifics.)
    3. Why did no-one notice and resolve the mistake before the event?
    I think this is an intriguing mistake because it’s clearly an interplay between an initial user mistake, a programming/system mistake, and another user mistake. Though whether any of these should actually be termed a mistake is a further topic of dialogue.
  2. It’s intriguing that the address is the correct address below the pic, i.e. City Hall, but the map indicates closer to County Hall. This implies to me that it wasn’t an initial user mistake.

    So did you look at the inaccurate map, skim read the address very rapidly and primed by the map understood it to be County Hall rather than City Hall.

    If the above is correct I think I would be less inclined to make the same mistake as the map and County Hall have less significance to me, i.e. I would be more dependent on the actual address and so more likely to head to City Hall (I think).

  3. Both are on The Queen’s Walk. Just at significantly different locations on that walkway. I don’t know where number 110 is, so the address doesn’t actually help clarify…

Honey - varieties and characteristics  

   Honey is one of the most precious nutrients, which nature provides us. Transforming them into the honey occurs in the bee body, and then on the combs. It involves the evaporation of moisture and several biochemical processes, including conversion of sucrose into glucose and fructose.  

   Flavor and fragrance of honey is determined by the elements of essential oils obtained from the nectar. Mature honey has the texture of thick syrup, which crystallize during preservation. The honey contains not too much of vitamins, but it is a source of large amounts of easily absorbable sugars, organic acids, mineral salts and various organic substances, particularly in combination with bee pollen and propolis (beneficial role of these two latter substances has not been fully clarified by researchers). It is extremely important that the honey shouldn’t be exposed to very high temperatures, destroying its bioactive substances. The ideal temperature at which honey should be prepared for therapeutic intents should not exceed 45 ° C. For optimal results, it is recommended to dissolve one teaspoon tablespoon of honey in warm water (half a cup) and leave for about 10-12 hours. The prepared beverage should be ingested with small spoons on an empty stomach. Furthermore, it is advised to keep the honey sealed, because honey absorbs humidity and external scents. Honey is best stored in a dry, ventilated area at 5-17 ° C.  

   The hue, scent, flavor and composition of honey relies primarily on the genus and species of plants from which bees gather nectar.  

Depending on the raw material from which the honey was produced, we distinguish the three basic types:  

- nectar honeys (flower)  
- honeydew honeys  
- mixed honey (honey-dew)  

Depending on the hue of honey, there are two types:  

- clear honey  
- dark honey

It has a reinforcing effect.  

Lime honey - (nectar, light) - the color of tea, linden flower fragrance, flavor spicy, bitter. Contains essential oils, saponins, vitamin C and other elements which aids in perspiration, antipyretic, expectorant and calming. It has a high antibiotic activity.  

Clover Honey - (nectar, clear) - white clover - a straw with a sweet taste of red clover - salmon, slightly tart. Faint scent of clover flowers. In this honey there is a lot of glycosides, alkaloids, coumarin, vitamins and pigments. Calming properties, is used in the treatment of nervous exhaustion and anemia.  

Raspberry Honey - (nectar, clear) - golden hue, the scent of tart raspberry flavor. It contains a lot of organic acids, including salicylic acid, a lot of pectin, and vitamins and many trace elements. It is used therapeutically in numerous diseases, including colds, flu, upper respiratory ailments, and atherosclerosis.  

Honey - (nectar, dark) - gathered from various herbs and plants. The most common is a light-brown, with an odor depending on the gathered nectar. Used for allergic ailments and respiratory system, such as asthma.  

Buckwheat honey - (nectar, dark) - the hue of amber or brown, with a strong scent of buckwheat flowers and sharp, slightly acrid flavor. It contains a large quantity of volatile compounds, derivatives of essential oils, minerals, enzymes, routine, inhibin, hormones. Used in cardiovascular ailments, atherosclerosis, impaired memory, after extensive efforts, or sickness and recovery.  

Heather honey - (nectar, dark) - the brown hue, with the aroma of heather flowers and a sharp, bitter flavor. Includes a lot of mineral salts, organic acids and tannins. Used in inflammation of the urinary system, kidney stones and intestinal inflammation.  

Honey from conifers - (honeydew, light) - is a gray-green, with the aroma of spicy, flavor mild, but very sweet. In this honey there is a larch sugar, much dextrin, nitrogen compounds and trace elements. Has anti-inflammatory, expectorant and antiseptic characteristics. Used with diminished immunity, diseases of the lungs, joints and nervous system. It prevents ionizing radiation.

Mixed - (mixed, dark) – brown-green hue, scent various, mostly spicy, very sweet. It has a high antibiotic activity.  

Contraindication to the consumption of honey is honey intolerance (allergy), and diabetes.
